resources.string: Requires disclosure acceptance — tap to review
When the Hotspot Gateway is enabled, this Android device will act as a network router for devices connected to its Wi-Fi hotspot.

Network traffic from connected devices (phones, laptops, smart TVs) will be forwarded through RNET\'s encrypted multi-path transport to the configured server endpoint. Connected devices do not need any additional software.

Non-identifying traffic statistics (byte counts, latency, connected device count) are logged locally on this device for bandwidth management and are not transmitted to any third party. No content of communications is inspected.
You can disable the Gateway at any time using the toggle on the main screen. All routing will stop immediately when you do so.
RNET will forward your network traffic through the nearby device "%1$s", which has an active internet connection. All traffic remains encrypted end-to-end. You can stop this at any time.
RNET will allow nearby devices in the local mesh cluster to route their traffic through this device\'s internet connection. All relayed traffic is encrypted. You can disable this at any time.
No traffic content is inspected. Only aggregate byte counts and latency are logged locally for bandwidth management.

When enabled, your traffic is routed through the Psiphon decentralized network (psiphon.ca) — an open-source, non-profit censorship-circumvention service. Psiphon can see that you are connected, but not the content of your traffic, which is end-to-end encrypted by RNET. Applies on next engine start.

Enter a valid hostname or IP

RNET is a multi-path encrypted transport tool. It routes your internet traffic through multiple cellular network paths simultaneously, using Reed-Solomon forward error correction (FEC) to recover lost packets. This makes the connection more reliable even in areas with poor coverage.
What does the "Multi-Path Transport" toggle do?

This is the main on/off switch. When you enable it, RNET starts a VPN tunnel on your device that captures all internet traffic and routes it through the configured relay server using an encrypted multi-path protocol. Android will show a VPN permission dialog on first use — this is required by Android for any app that creates a VPN connection.

When this is enabled, your traffic is routed through the Psiphon decentralized network (psiphon.ca) before reaching the relay server. Psiphon is an open-source, non-profit censorship-circumvention service operated by Psiphon Inc., a Canadian non-profit. Use this option if your connection to the relay server is blocked or throttled. Psiphon can see that you are connected, but not the content of your traffic, which is end-to-end encrypted by RNET.

The Hotspot Gateway lets other devices (phones, laptops, tablets) connect to your phone\'s Wi-Fi hotspot and route their traffic through RNET. This is useful when you need to share a protected connection. It requires explicit consent because it routes third-party traffic — you must accept the disclosure screen before it can be enabled. All traffic remains encrypted.
What does the Link Telemetry section show?

• Signal Quality (SNR) — an estimate of your cellular signal strength, derived from RSRP (Reference Signal Received Power). 
• Packet Delivery Rate — the percentage of data packets that arrive successfully. 
• Radio Technology — the current mobile network type (LTE, 5G, etc.) and band. 
• Active Stations — the number of devices currently routed through the Hotspot Gateway. 
• Data Received / Sent — total bytes transferred during this session.
How do I set up a relay server?

RNET requires a self-hosted relay server. You can deploy one on any Linux VPS (DigitalOcean, Hetzner, Vultr, etc.) with a single command:

 docker compose up

Run this in the deploy/ directory of the RNET repository. Then enter the server's IP address and port (default 7777) in the RNET Setup screen. If no relay is configured, RNET will fall back to Psiphon as the upstream transport.
Why does RNET ask for VPN permission?

Android requires explicit user approval before any app can create a VPN tunnel. This is a security feature built into Android. RNET uses the VPN interface only to capture traffic and route it through the configured relay server — it does not connect to any external VPN provider.

Your traffic is encrypted end-to-end between your device and the relay server using AES-256-GCM. The relay server you configure is under your control. If you also enable Resilient Core (Psiphon), Psiphon can see your connection metadata (IP address, timing) but not the content of your traffic. RNET itself does not log or transmit any traffic data to Anthropic or any other third party.
What do I do if the VPN permission dialog crashes the app?

This was a known issue in earlier versions caused by a timing problem in the Psiphon startup sequence. It has been fixed. If you experience a crash, please restart the app and try again. If it persists, go to Android Settings → Apps → RNET → Permissions and check that VPN permission is not permanently denied.
How do I completely stop RNET?

Toggle the "Multi-Path Transport" switch to OFF on the main screen. You can also tap "Stop" in the RNET notification in your notification shade. The VPN tunnel and all background services will stop immediately.
